examples.solution_text:
The top entry is the horizontal component and the bottom entry is the vertical component.
$\begin{pmatrix}-5\\9\end{pmatrix}=-5\underset{\sim}{i}+9\underset{\sim}{j}$

Put the coefficient of $\underset{\sim}{i}$ above the coefficient of $\underset{\sim}{j}$, keeping their signs.
$8\underset{\sim}{i}-5\underset{\sim}{j}=\begin{pmatrix}8\\-5\end{pmatrix}$

examples.question_text:
(a) Write $-5\underset{\sim}{i}$ as a column vector.
(b) Write $\begin{pmatrix}0\\4\end{pmatrix}$ in component form.
examples.solution_text:
(a) There is no $\underset{\sim}{j}$ term, so the vertical component is zero.
$-5\underset{\sim}{i}=\begin{pmatrix}-5\\0\end{pmatrix}$

(b) The horizontal component is zero, so omit the $\underset{\sim}{i}$ term.
$\begin{pmatrix}0\\4\end{pmatrix}=4\underset{\sim}{j}$

Use horizontal then vertical order. The coefficient of $-\underset{\sim}{j}$ is $-1$.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}-\underset{\sim}{j}+11\underset{\sim}{i}\\&=11\underset{\sim}{i}-\underset{\sim}{j}\\&=\begin{pmatrix}11\\-1\end{pmatrix}\end{aligned}$

coverage.summary: Authored five examples covering every distinct assessed method, using adapted booklet values. Prompts and solutions are separate; solution prose remains editable and inherits renderer blue. The continuation chain has a phantom equals gutter. Editable diagrams keep component annotations in the solution only, with standard colours and declared label sizes. Assessments were classified solely for coverage and were neither changed nor re-audited. Independent example review and actual rendered verification remain later stages.

examples.derivation: The column entries give horizontal coefficient -5 and vertical coefficient 9, so the component form is -5i + 9j. This follows the conversions at source lines 1897–1902.
The i coefficient is 8 and the j coefficient is -5, giving the column (8,-5). This follows source lines 1904–1906.

In (a), -5i has horizontal component -5 and vertical component 0, giving (-5,0). In (b), (0,4) has no horizontal term and becomes 4j. Source lines 1888–1891 and 1917–1939 support these zero-component conversions.

Identifying coefficients by basis vector gives horizontal component 11 and vertical component -1, hence (11,-1). Reordering preserves the vector. The opening expression has the required phantom equals gutter; source lines 1904–1906 and 1929–1931 support the method.

Tail (3,2) to tip (-1,-1) gives horizontal movement -1-3=-4 and vertical movement -1-2=-3. Thus the column is (-4,-3) and component form is -4i-3j. The solution arrows reproduce these movements tip to tail. Supplied images 20, 21 and 26–31 support decomposition and signed geometric conversion.
